neighbours.label: position just before a non-English language or nationality name in contexts of ethnic minorities and language assimilation (use of ___, changed into ___, spoke perfect ___)
fire: The Basque villagers were fined whenever they refused to speak only Castilian.
After the annexation, Korean family names had to be rewritten into Japanese.
Armenian refugees who settled in Aleppo soon learned to speak fluent Arabic.
Officials complained about the Sorbs' stubborn use of their Slavic dialect instead of German.
Tensions rose between native Tatars and newly arrived settlers who spoke only Russian.
The Berber children were punished at school unless they answered in perfect French.
Thousands of Rohingya fled across the border and were told to register in Bengali.
The decree required that all Kurdish village names be changed into Turkish.
quiet: The villagers were fined whenever they refused to pay the bridge toll.
After the flood, family records had to be rewritten into new ledgers.
Students who settled in the dormitory soon learned to cook simple meals.
Officials complained about the farmers' stubborn use of old wooden ploughs.
Tensions rose between the miners and newly arrived managers who cut wages.
The children were punished at school unless they answered in complete sentences.
Thousands of fans crossed the bridge and were told to register at the gate.
The decree required that all village wells be covered with stone lids.

notes: Card: peaks on ' of', ' into', ' to', ' and', ' perfect' before Arabic / Chinese / German in passages on Moriscos, Uyghurs, Kurds, Jews; the + pole's output promotes ' English', so this pole suppresses it. Probe: 'speak only [Spanish]' 0.41, 'converted into [Mandarin]' 0.32, 'fled to [Turkey]' 0.27; non-ethnic control 0.06, English-speaking tourists 0.01.
